requirement: TypeScript and TSX report `Comment` and `Annotation` attachments.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments` has one obligation. TypeScript and TSX outlines must report both `Comment` and `Annotation` attachments. The test is `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. It carries a {test} reference to the subject, and it covers both languages: - **`test.ts`:** The source is `/** doc */\nconst s = '// string'; // trailing\n@dec class C {}\n`. The test asserts exactly `[(Comment, "/** doc */"), (Comment, "// trailing"), (Annotation, "@dec")]`. That shows a block comment and a line comment reported as `Comment`, and a decorator reported as `Annotation`. - **`test.tsx`:** The source is `/* doc */\nconst s =

// text

; // trailing\n@dec class C {}\n`. The test asserts exactly `[(Comment, "/* doc */"), (Comment, "// trailing"), (Annotation, "@dec")]`. So the TSX grammar is exercised separately and reports both kinds. The assertion is an exact-equality check on kind and text, so a wrong kind, a missing attachment or a spurious one would fail it. The string `'// string'` and the JSX text `// text` are not reported, so the test also rules out treating them as comments. The refining requirements `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments.comments`, `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments.decorators` and `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments.decorators.span` hold the finer obligations. These cover comment attachment rules and decorator spans. They are assessed under their own references, not here.

text: TypeScript and TSX report `Comment` and `Annotation` attachments.
